explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/79: are there infinitely many graphs G that are not Ramsey size linear but all of whose (proper) subgraphs are? (yes, Wigderson). The Lean statement asserts, for every N, a graph G on Fin n with n ≥ N that is not IsRamseySizeLinear while every proper subgraph H < ⊤ (as a graph on its own vertex set) is. Requiring arbitrarily large n is equivalent to infinitely many such graphs (finitely many graphs per order), and it cannot be met trivially by padding with isolated vertices: deleting an isolated vertex does not change Ramsey size linearity, so a minimal example has none. 'Subgraphs' is correctly read as proper subgraphs. Faithful.
